title: Iron Man: Rise of Technovore
edition: 2013 Madhouse animated feature, North American English-language direct-to-video release.
synopsis: Tony Stark believes Rhodey has died during an attack on a satellite launch. He evades questioning and follows the weapons trail with Frank Castle, whose treatment of a suspect forces Tony to intervene.
verdictRationale: Tony interrupts Castle before he kills a witness. He needs information, so the rescue is an imperfect act of mercy. His strongest choice comes later when he gives Rhodey the power to put Tony himself in danger to save others. The film admires that trust while also making an armed pursuit driven by revenge exciting.
ageRationale: Sustained animated gunfire and explosions accompany a friend’s apparent death and the loss of control over a living body. A younger teen disturbed by body horror or bereavement may want to skip it.
reflection: Tony starts out trying to act for a friend he believes he has lost. At the end he has to act with that friend and accept help himself. Trust becomes harder, and more meaningful, when Rhodey must make the decision Tony cannot make for him.

themes.name: Self-sacrifice
themes.evidence: Tony deliberately puts his own life within the satellite’s line of fire. His choice makes the final rescue possible.

themes.name: Restraint
themes.evidence: Tony interrupts an execution, but his immediate purpose is to question the prisoner. This moment of restraint has limits.

themes.name: Domination
themes.evidence: Ezekiel plans to replace humanity and then loses command of his own body. The danger of control shapes both the threat and its outcome.

title: Avengers Confidential: Black Widow & Punisher
edition: 2014 Madhouse animated feature directed by Kenichi Shimizu, North American English-language home-video release.
synopsis: Natasha Romanoff and Frank Castle track stolen S.H.I.E.L.D. technology to an auction of captive super-soldiers. One of the people responsible is a scientist Natasha once loved.
verdictRationale: Natasha asks what control Frank had over his actions before allowing him to be judged for killing agents. Elihas eventually turns on the project he helped create and takes a fatal blow for her. Yet the ending gives Frank freedom to kill again. His execution of Cain leaves a serious question about the kind of justice the heroes have accepted.
ageRationale: The sustained action includes a brainwashed ally killing his own side, a fatal attack in front of a loved one and a final vigilante killing. Following the difference between coercion and a freely chosen act matters more here than familiarity with the Avengers.
reflection: Natasha grants Frank the hearing she would want for someone she loved. Her later decision to release him raises a harder pastoral question. What does mercy ask of us when someone we defend still intends to hurt another person?

themes.name: Self-sacrifice
themes.evidence: Elihas first helps disable his soldiers and then shields Natasha at the cost of his life. The climax gives his change of allegiance a cost.

themes.name: Fair judgment
themes.evidence: Natasha challenges the decision to imprison Frank when evidence suggests another person controlled his actions.

themes.name: Vigilante killing
themes.evidence: Frank’s lethal methods cause friction with S.H.I.E.L.D., yet he is released and his killing of Cain supplies the ending.

themes.name: Coercion
themes.evidence: The auction treats captive people as weapons. Mind control also turns Frank against his allies, making lost agency central to the story.
